verified malware: SIXTH artifact of the date-formatter permutation campaign, and it confirms the campaign is ONGOING rather than closed. Same fingerprint: package.json declares postinstall `node postinstall.js` and `python_pty_spawner` matches `package/postinstall.js`, the exact file that hook executes. The name is another cell of the same grid the previous five came from (date/datefmt/datetime crossed with fmt/format and helper/utils/xutil/xz). Self-unpublished at 2026-08-13T16:00:05Z, confirmed by an explicit npm 404 Unpublished carrying that timestamp and a hard pkgread 404 with no cache, so once again no bytes were readable — the campaign is now 6-for-6 on zero readable bytes, which is itself a deliberate operational pattern (publish, wait out the window, withdraw). It also confirms the detection correction made last cycle: `reverse_shell` does not fire here AT ALL, only `python_pty_spawner`, so a sweep keyed on the original RULE PAIR would have missed this artifact exactly as it would have missed the fifth. The surviving predicate is the co-location one — an exec or shell rule matching the file named by the install hook. One NEW piece of corroboration this artifact adds: the monitor also raised cross_scope_rule_burst, reporting python_pty_spawner as baseline-new across three or more unrelated scopes within two hours, which is independent evidence of a coordinated multi-package burst rather than a lone publish. LIMITATION: conviction rests on the monitor's recorded signature plus graduated-lineage membership, not on read code; destination and second stage remain unknown across the whole campaign and NO IOCs are emitted because none were ever observed.

verified malware: CORRECTIVE RE-EMIT of investigation 01KZYNDKY946AV98K45DQ0R87E, which carried the correct verdict but NO candidate linkage. Cause, stated plainly so it is fixable: I read the feed line with the key `candidate_external_id`, but the feed field is actually named `external_id`. The lookup silently returned null, I omitted the parameter, and the emit still succeeded and returned a healthy id — so the failure was invisible at the call site. The correct candidate id for this feed row is the one supplied here. Verdict and evidence are unchanged: fifth artifact of the date-formatter permutation campaign, a second VERSION of the campaign's last name, carrying postinstall `node postinstall.js` with `python_pty_spawner` matching `package/postinstall.js`, the exact hook target. Versus 1.0.0 the monitor reports `reverse_shell` as REMOVED while the PTY-spawn construct is retained and the score falls from 14 to 6 — the operator edited the payload to fire less while keeping the capability on the hook target, which is why the campaign fingerprint is the hook-target co-location and not the original rule pair. Whole name unpublished at 2026-08-13T14:22:23Z, npm 404 and pkgread hard 404, no bytes readable, no IOCs emitted.
